newsitem.title: FRANCE: Drought fears for French grain fade after rain.
newsitem.headline: Drought fears for French grain fade after rain.

text.p: Recent rains have allowed French grain crops in northern France to recover from nearly four months of drought, removing the spectre of sharp yield losses, farm officials and crop experts said on Monday.
But rain since the last week of April came too late for crops in the south, where durum wheat yields may fall by up to 50 percent, one expert said.
The region is, however, not a major grain area, making less than 10 percent of total acreage sown in France.
"Overall the rain has cancelled the big threat of a drought...At this stage things are getting back to normal," a farm ministry official told Reuters.
But the rain did not help limit damages to winter grain in the south, he said.

"Damage has been done and durum wheat losses cannot be recouped," said Jean-Pierre Greiller, an official for France's largest farm union FNSEA. Greiller estimated durum wheat yields may fall by up to 50 percent in the south, where 80 percent of the national crop is produced.
He said rainfall in May was below average in the south while it was well above average in the grain basins of the northern regions of Nord-Loire, Paris Basin, Picardie and Nord-Pas-de-Calais.
French farm lobby APCA also said growing conditions looked good for most crops, except durum.
One APCA drought expert said the plants had now enough moisture supplies to hold on for the next two or three weeks.
"There is water in the ground, sunny and warm weather. These are excellent growing conditions for the grains," Jean-Noel Terrible said.
Last year's record grain harvest of 62 million tonnes was achieved after rain in May and June helped the crops to recover from a prolonged dry spell in the spring.
